how_to_enable: an operator must restart the server with --enable-control AND set "control": true on the camera's config entry
explanation: when control is disabled, the write tools listed in gated_write_tools are not registered and do not appear in tools/list; when enabled the write tools still default to dry_run true (the halt tools do not, see below), so a caller must pass dry_run false to change a camera, and only cameras with control_allowed true accept it. control_allowed is a camera's own opt-in and only takes effect when control_enabled is true; writable says whether a camera can be controlled now. ptz.stop stops motion and is listed in gated_write_tools too, but has no dry run and is not rate limited: it is available whenever control is enabled and the camera opted in, so a stop is never held back by the movement rate limit
why: write tools physically move or reconfigure a real camera; an agent that loops on them can wear out or wedge the mechanism, so they are off unless an operator opts in
